summary: George Lakoff is a linguist and philosopher who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (~1959–1962) and Indiana University (~1962–1966). He held a post at the University of California, Berkeley from around 1972 to 2016.

George Melville Bolling worked in Indology and linguistics. Educated at Loyola University Maryland (~1887–1891) and Johns Hopkins University (~1891–1896), he held posts at Catholic University of America (1895–1913), Johns Hopkins (1913–1914), and Ohio State University (1914–1939).

George Peiris Malalasekera worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics, studying under Caroline A. F. Rhys Davids and William Stede at SOAS and the University of London. He held posts at Ceylon University College (~1927–1942) and the University of Ceylon (~1942–1957).
George R. Elder worked in Buddhist studies and religious studies, studying at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Alex Wayman (attested 1978).

George Roerich specialized in Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied under Lobsang Mingyur Dorje, at the University of London (~1919–1920), and Harvard University (~1920–1922), later serving at the Institute of Oriental Studies (~1957–1960).

Philosopher George Santayana studied at Harvard College, the Humboldt University of Berlin, King's College, and Harvard University under William James. He held a post at Harvard University from around 1889 to 1912.
George Sessions was a philosopher who held posts at Sierra College from 1992 to 1993 and as attested in 2002.
George Shirt was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Cambridge (graduating in 1864) and Church Missionary Society College, Islington (~1864–1866).

George Thibaut worked in Indology, studying under Albrecht Weber in 1867. He served as Direktor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1879–1888), Principal at Muir Central College (~1888–1906), and held a post at the University of Calcutta (~1906–1914).
George Watt studied at the University of Aberdeen (~1868–1871) and the University of Glasgow (~1871–1873). He subsequently held a post at the University of Calcutta from around 1873 to 1884.

George van Driem is a linguist and Tibetologist who completed his doctorate at Leiden University (~1983–1987). He held posts at Leiden University (~1987–2009), the University of Bern (2010–2022), and IIT Guwahati (2020).

Georges Dreyfus works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under various traditional teachers, at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, and at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, later holding posts at Virginia and Williams College.

Georges-Jean Pinault is a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied at École Normale Supérieure (1974). He held posts at Blaise Pascal University (~1988–1994) and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1999).

Georgios T. Halkias works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Hawaii and University of Oxford under Charles Ramble, holding posts at the Warburg Institute, SOAS, Ruhr University Bochum, and the University of Hong Kong (~2014).

Gerald James Larson worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, having studied at Union Theological Seminary and Columbia University. He served as professor at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1970–1995) and Indiana University (~1995–2003).

Gereon Kopf works in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Temple University and under Yasuo Yuasa, holding posts at J. F. Oberlin University, Luther College, Nanzan Institute for Religion and Culture, and the University of Hong Kong.

Gergely Hidas is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned his doctorate at Balliol College, Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He held posts at Eötvös Loránd University (2007–2014) and the British Museum (2014).

Gerhard Oberhammer was an Indologist, philosopher, and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Innsbruck, under Erich Frauwallner, V. Raghavan, and at the University of Paris, later holding posts at Utrecht University (1961) and the University of Vienna (1964).

Geshe Gendun Lodro worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Drepung Gomang Dratsang under Khensur Ngawang Lekden and held posts at Drepung Gomang Dratsang, the University of Hamburg (1967), and the University of Virginia (~1979).
Geshe Karma Sonam is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held posts at Gyume Tantric College (attested 1987) and Sera Monastery (attested 1992).
